briefing:
### The window in one sentence

The seven days ending August 5 produced 157 sessions at a 22.4/day average, with Organic Search leading traffic in an unexpected reversal of BCC's usual Direct-first pattern. The window is genuinely accelerating -- pageviews nearly doubled from first half to second half -- though a mid-week valley on August 1-2 and zero GSC data complicate the read.

---

### Volume + composition

Over the July 30 -- August 5 window, the site recorded 157 sessions, 143 users, and 567 pageviews across seven days. Per-day averages came in at 22.4 sessions and 20.4 users, which sits modestly above the implied 28-day median of roughly 19-20 sessions/day. GSC impressions and clicks show zero for the entire window -- this is almost certainly a data pipeline issue rather than a ranking collapse, given the 415K+ impressions attributed in the 30-day efficacy rollup. That GSC gap needs to be resolved before you can draw any meaningful search-visibility conclusions from this period.

Channel composition flipped BCC's baseline in a notable way. Organic Search drove 83 sessions (53% of total), while Direct came in at 53 sessions (34%) -- nearly the inverse of the expected ~60% Direct / ~25% Organic split. Referral added 15 sessions (10%), Organic Social contributed 5, and Email just 1. The Organic Search dominance is the most meaningful signal here: it suggests either a real ranking improvement on one or more pages, or that a Direct traffic source that usually gets misattributed as Direct is temporarily absent (a paused email newsletter, for example). The Referral share is right on baseline at 10%, which is unremarkable.

The August 5 anomaly -- 162 pageviews on 23 sessions, producing an average session duration of 408 seconds (240% above the 28-day median) -- is the standout data point. People who came that day stayed and read deeply. That is not bot traffic; that is genuine engagement. Worth investigating which pages drove that depth, likely the GLP-1 medication content or one of the core service pages.

---

### Trend (first half vs second half)

The halves comparison shows a 6.6% session uptick (76 sessions in the first three days vs. 81 in the last four), which on its own sounds modest. But the pageview story is considerably more interesting: 207 pageviews in the first half vs. 360 in the second half -- a 74% jump. That gap between session growth and pageview growth means visitors in the second half of the window were consuming significantly more content per visit, consistent with the spiking average session duration on August 4-5.

The mid-week trough (August 1: 10 sessions, August 2: 12 sessions) was flagged as CRITICAL and MAJOR across all metrics, running 40-63% below the 28-day median. That valley lands on a Saturday/Sunday, which is consistent with BCC's audience behaving like a healthcare-seeking weekday audience. The recovery from Sunday's trough back to 19 (Monday), 27 (Tuesday), and 23 (Wednesday) suggests the underlying trend is intact. The window is accelerating in quality of engagement, if not dramatically in raw session volume.

---

### Launches + efficacy

All ten tracked launches -- six page modifications and four post modifications -- went live on August 6, which is one day after the window closes. That means none of the launch activity drove traffic within this measurement window. Those pages are too fresh (one day live as of today) to draw efficacy conclusions yet; check back in the next 7-14 day window for meaningful signals.

That said, the cumulative GSC data attached to those pages tells a useful pre-modification story about what they were doing before the edits shipped. The GLP-1 medications page (/understanding-weight-loss-medications-wegovy-ozempic-zepbound-and-mounjaro/) carries 28,477 lifetime GSC impressions and 42 GA4 sessions -- that is by far the highest-traffic content piece in the top launches list. Its 0.3% CTR is low for the impression volume it's earning, which suggests the title or meta description may not be compelling enough to earn the click even when Google is serving it. The homepage (/) shows 99,821 impressions and 629 sessions at a 0.6% CTR -- healthy volume but the CTR has room to grow. The About page (/about/) is the relative CTR leader at 1.0% on 6,677 impressions. The Bariatric Surgery Counseling page (/bariatric-surgery-counseling-in-san-antonio-tx/) has earned 1,609 impressions with zero clicks -- that zero-click pattern is a flag worth revisiting once the August 6 edits have had two weeks to settle.

Four post modifications (self-sabotage, goal-setting, emotional eating, and BCC in the News) show zero GSC impressions and zero GA4 sessions as of today. At one day live, that is expected -- GSC lag is typically 3-7 days minimum. These are not yet underperforming; they simply have not had time to register.

Backlinks look solid at a baseline level: 4 referring domains, 12 inbound links, and 5 .edu links. No competitor links, which is the right answer. The .edu count is worth tracking -- educational institution links carry significant authority weight for a practice that operates in a clinical-adjacent space.

---

### What this means + what to do next

1. **Investigate the August 5 depth spike before it gets buried.** The 408-second average session duration on August 5 is the most meaningful engagement signal in this window. Pull the page-level report for that date and identify which specific pages held attention that long. If it was the GLP-1 medication content, that page cluster deserves internal linking priority immediately -- deep engagement combined with strong impression volume suggests it can convert more of those impressions into leads.

2. **Fix the GSC data pipeline.** Seven consecutive days of zero impressions in the aggregate is a data issue, not a ranking issue. Resolve the GSC connection before the next rollup so the August 6 launch batch has a clean data environment to measure into. Without GSC data you are flying partially blind on search performance.

3. **Plan a CTR audit on the GLP-1 page and the Bariatric Surgery Counseling page.** The GLP-1 page is earning 28K impressions at 0.3% CTR and the surgery counseling page earned 1,609 impressions with zero clicks. Both have had modifications just deployed -- in 10-14 days, run a before/after CTR comparison. If the rewrites did not move CTR, the title tags and meta descriptions likely need another pass specifically written for the search snippet context, not the page heading.

4. **Build out the Organic Search advantage while it's present.** Organic Search delivered 53% of sessions this window versus an expected 25%. If this holds in the next rollup, it suggests one or more pages climbed in rankings. Identify those pages now (once GSC is repaired) and add internal links from the homepage and high-traffic service pages pointing to them -- capitalize on the momentum before it normalizes.

5. **Give the August 6 post modifications (self-sabotage, goal-setting, emotional eating) two weeks before evaluating.** Do not optimize or re-modify these posts based on week-one data. Set a calendar reminder to review them in the August 21 rollup window with GSC impression and ranking data in hand. If they still show zero impressions at that point, request manual indexing through Google Search Console.
